summary: Woensdrecht Air Base is a Royal Netherlands Air Force military installation located near Hoogerheide in the southern Dutch province of North Brabant, just a few kilometers from the Belgian border. The base has historically operated F-16 Fighting Falcon squadrons and has roots dating back to World War II, when the airfield was used by German forces. Today it serves military aviation purposes while also accommodating limited civil and general aviation traffic.
faqs:
Q: Is Woensdrecht Air Base open to civilian passengers?
A: No, Woensdrecht is primarily a military facility with very limited public access; travelers cannot book regular commercial flights here.

Q: Which military aircraft have been based at Woensdrecht?
A: The base has long hosted Royal Netherlands Air Force F-16 Fighting Falcon squadrons and has served as a key operational and training airfield.

Q: How close is Woensdrecht to major cities?
A: The base is roughly 25 km west of Breda, close to Bergen op Zoom, and within easy driving distance of the Belgian city of Antwerp.

Q: Can the public visit the air base?
A: The base occasionally opens to the public during special events or open days hosted by the Royal Netherlands Air Force, but access is normally restricted.
transport_tips: A private car is the most practical way to reach Woensdrecht Air Base, as it lies directly off the A58 motorway between Bergen op Zoom and the Belgian border. Public transport options are limited, with bus services serving nearby villages and the closest train station located in Bergen op Zoom. Visitors coming from Belgium can easily access the base via the A4 motorway connecting Antwerp to the Dutch south.
